column3: The Hebrew names the sea as the fourth direction; BSB says south.
The Hebrew says they found no dwelling city; BSB describes finding no path to such a city.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats soul for the thirsty and hungry; BSB omits the noun.
The Hebrew names iron rather than chains.
The Hebrew has a singular heart; BSB has hearts.
The Hebrew has a singular way of their transgression; BSB has rebellious ways.
The Hebrew makes their soul the subject that loathes food; BSB says they loathed it.
The Hebrew has their pits in the plural; BSB has the Pit.
The Hebrew describes going down to sea and doing work; BSB says going out and conducting trade.
The Hebrew names their soul; BSB says their courage.
The Hebrew compares them with a singular drunkard and describes their wisdom being swallowed; BSB has drunkards and skill being useless.
The Hebrew names silence and their waves without explicitly naming sea; BSB says whisper and waves of the sea.
